es: Más vale tarde que nunca.
en: Better late than never.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente.
en: Out of sight, out of mind.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho.
en: There is a long way between saying and doing.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Más vale prevenir que curar.
en: Prevention is better than cure.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Donde hay voluntad, hay camino.
en: Where there is a will, there is a way.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Quien no arriesga, no gana.
en: Whoever does not take risks does not win.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Poco a poco se va lejos.
en: Little by little one goes far.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Nunca es tarde si la dicha es buena.
en: It is never too late if the outcome is good.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: La práctica hace al maestro.
en: Practice makes the master.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta.
en: Whoever grasps too much holds little.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: No hay mal que por bien no venga.
en: No evil comes without some good.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Más vale solo que mal acompañado.
en: Better to be alone than in bad company.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: En la variedad está el gusto.
en: Variety is the spice of life.
source: Traditional Spanish saying, anonymous

es: La necesidad obliga.
en: Necessity compels.
source: Traditional Spanish saying, anonymous

es: Más vale un ave en mano que cien volando.
en: A bird in the hand is worth a hundred flying.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: No juzgues un libro por su portada.
en: Do not judge a book by its cover.
source: Traditional Spanish saying, anonymous

es: Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.
en: Tell me who you walk with and I will tell you who you are.
source: Traditional Spanish saying, anonymous

es: El que mucho habla, mucho yerra.
en: Whoever talks a lot makes many mistakes.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda.
en: God helps the one who rises early.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: Después de la lluvia, sale el sol.
en: After the rain, the sun comes out.
source: Traditional Spanish refrán, anonymous

es: A buen hambre no hay pan duro.
en: Hunger is the best sauce.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: En boca cerrada no entran moscas.
en: A closed mouth catches no flies.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Adonde fueres, haz como vieres.
en: Wherever you go, do as you find.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Cría cuervos y te sacarán los ojos.
en: Raise crows and they will peck out your eyes.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: No hay peor sordo que el que no quiere oír.
en: There is no worse deaf person than one who refuses to hear.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: El que siembra vientos, recoge tempestades.
en: Whoever sows the wind reaps the storm.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Dios ayuda a los que se ayudan.
en: God helps those who help themselves.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Un clavo saca otro clavo.
en: One nail drives out another.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Año nuevo, vida nueva.
en: New year, new life.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: A mal tiempo, buena cara.
en: Keep a good face in bad times.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: A palabras necias, oídos sordos.
en: To foolish words, deaf ears.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: De la discusión brota la luz.
en: Light comes out of discussion.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: A Dios rogando y con el mazo dando.
en: Pray to God, but keep swinging the hammer.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: El que anda con la miel, algo se le pega.
en: You cannot touch honey without getting sticky.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Zapatero, a tus zapatos.
en: Cobbler, stick to your last.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: La ocasión hace al ladrón.
en: Opportunity makes the thief.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: No hay peor ciego que el que no quiere ver.
en: There is no worse blind person than one who refuses to see.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Comida hecha, compañía deshecha.
en: Once the meal is done, the guests depart.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Quien abrojos siembra, espinas coge.
en: Whoever sows thorns gathers prickles.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous

es: Aceituna, una es oro, dos plata, y la tercera, mata.
en: One olive is gold, two are silver, and the third kills you.
source: Sbarbi y Osuna, Diccionario de refranes (1922); traditional refrán, anonymous
